title: Augmented injective coresolutions detect Ext of cycles
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $T\in\mathcal A$, and fix an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $0\to T\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$. Define the acyclic integer cochain complex $E(T)$ by $E(T)^0=T$, $E(T)^{k+1}=I^k$ for $k\geq0$, and $E(T)^k=0$ for $k<0$, with differential $\varepsilon$ in degree zero and the resolution differentials thereafter. Let $X=(X^n,d_X^n)_{n\in\mathbf Z}$ be an integer cochain complex, meaning $d_X^{n+1}d_X^n=0$, that is acyclic, meaning $\operatorname{im}d_X^{n-1}=\ker d_X^n$ in every degree, and assume $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(X^1,T)=0$, where $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ denotes isomorphism classes of short exact extension sequences (short exactness is as in [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]) with the Baer addition; the displayed vanishing means that every short exact extension of $X^1$ by $T$ splits. Put $Z^nX=\ker d_X^n$. With $\operatorname{Hom}^r(X,E(T))=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(X^n,E(T)^{n+r})$ and differential $\delta h=d_Eh-(-1)^rhd_X$, define $H^0\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(X,E(T))$ as $\ker(\delta:\operatorname{Hom}^0\to\operatorname{Hom}^1)/\operatorname{im}(\delta:\operatorname{Hom}^{-1}\to\operatorname{Hom}^0)$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$H^0\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(X,E(T))\cong\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(Z^2X,T).$$
For a cochain map $f:X\to E(T)$, the corresponding extension class is the pushout of $0\to Z^1X\to X^1\to Z^2X\to0$ along the unique map $Z^1X\to T$ through which $f^0:X^0\to T$ factors via $d_X^0:X^0\twoheadrightarrow Z^1X$; the isomorphism is natural under cochain maps of such acyclic sources and morphisms of augmented injective resolutions (with the displayed Ext-one vanishing for each source involved).

proof.text: Write $i_n:Z^nX\hookrightarrow X^n$ for the kernel inclusion and $p_n:X^n\twoheadrightarrow Z^{n+1}X$ for the differential with its codomain restricted to its image; thus $d_X^n=i_{n+1}p_n$. Acyclicity and the exactness definition give $\operatorname{im}d_X^{n-1}=Z^nX$. To check that $p_n$ is epic without an elementwise-surjectivity assumption, take $y:D\to Z^{n+1}X$. Exactness and part (b) of the refinement lemma lift $i_{n+1}y$ through $d_X^n$ after an epimorphism $\rho:D'\twoheadrightarrow D$. Cancelling $i_{n+1}$ gives a lift of $y\rho$ through $p_n$. Part (a) of that lemma makes $p_n$ epic. Consequently $0\to Z^nX\xrightarrow{i_n}X^n\xrightarrow{p_n}Z^{n+1}X\to0$ is short exact for every $n$. By the cited cokernel statement, $p_n$ is a cokernel of $i_n$; every map out of $X^n$ killing $i_n$ therefore factors uniquely through $p_n$. The same resolution exactness says that $E(T)$ is acyclic: in degree zero $\varepsilon$ is monic, in positive degrees its consecutive images equal kernels, and all negative terms are zero.

proof.text: Let $M$ be the abelian group of cochain maps $X\to E(T)$. In degree zero, $\delta f=0$ is precisely $d_E^nf^n=f^{n+1}d_X^n$ for all $n$. In degree minus one, $\delta h=d_Eh+hd_X$. Thus $H^0\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(X,E(T))=M/\{d_Eh+hd_X\}$, with the operations induced by addition of maps. This is a substitution into the differential specified in the statement, and fixes the homotopy sign.

source.place: Agent calculation below proof paragraph 2: degree-zero cocycles and degree-minus-one coboundaries.

proof.text: For $f\in M$, the degree-minus-one chain equation says $f^0d_X^{-1}=0$. Since $d_X^{-1}=i_0p_{-1}$ with $p_{-1}$ epic, $f^0i_0=0$. Step 1 gives a unique $g_f:Z^1X\to T$ with $f^0=g_fp_0$. This assignment $r:M\to\operatorname{Hom}(Z^1X,T)$ is additive, by uniqueness of factorization. To lift a given $g$, set $f^0=gp_0$ and all $f^n=0$ for $n<0$; these satisfy the chain equations in negative degrees.

source.place: Agent calculation below proof paragraph 2: the factor through the first cycle and the initial values for upward induction.

proof.text: Suppose $n\ge0$ and the components $f^k$ through $n$ have been chosen with the chain equations in degrees $k<n$. Put $w=d_E^nf^n$. Then $w d_X^{n-1}=d_E^nd_E^{n-1}f^{n-1}=0$ (at $n=0$ this follows also from $f^0i_0=0$). Cancel the epic $p_{n-1}$ to get $wi_n=0$, and factor $w=v_np_n$ by Step 1. The target of $v_n:Z^{n+1}X\to E(T)^{n+1}=I^n$ is injective, so extend $v_n$ along $i_{n+1}$ to $f^{n+1}:X^{n+1}\to I^n$. Then $f^{n+1}d_X^n=f^{n+1}i_{n+1}p_n=v_np_n=d_E^nf^n$. Ordinary induction on $n$ gives a cochain map with $r(f)=g$; in particular $r$ is surjective. For $n=0$, $v_0=\varepsilon g$, so this is the promised extension of the prescribed augmentation data.

source.place: Agent proof below proof paragraph 2: injective extension at each positive degree. Injectivity is the extension property in def-sp-injective-resolutions; no boundedness of X or enough injectives for other objects is used.

proof.text: If $k=f'-f=d_Eh+hd_X$, then $E(T)^{-1}=0$ gives $k^0=h^1d_X^0$. Cancelling $p_0$ in $g_kp_0=h^1i_1p_0$ gives $g_{f'}-g_f=h^1i_1$. Conversely suppose $g_{f'}-g_f=ui_1$ for $u:X^1\to T$. Put $h^n=0$ for $n\le0$ and $h^1=u$. Then $k^0=h^1d_X^0$, and the homotopy equations hold in every degree at most zero.

source.place: Agent proof below proof paragraph 2: necessary restriction condition for a homotopy, and its initial degree-zero equation.

proof.text:
For the converse in Step 5, suppose $n\ge1$, $h^n$ has been chosen, and $k^j=d_E^{j-1}h^j+h^{j+1}d_X^j$ for all $j<n$. Define $w_n=k^n-d_E^{n-1}h^n$. Since $k$ is a cochain map, $w_nd_X^{n-1}=d_E^{n-1}(k^{n-1}-h^nd_X^{n-1})=d_E^{n-1}d_E^{n-2}h^{n-1}=0$. Thus $w_ni_n=0$, and $w_n=v_np_n$. Now $E(T)^n=I^{n-1}$ is injective, so extend $v_n$ along $i_{n+1}$ to $h^{n+1}:X^{n+1}\to E(T)^n$. This gives the next homotopy equation. Induction constructs all components. It follows from Steps 3–6 that the rule $[f]\mapsto[g_f]$ is a well-defined bijective homomorphism
$$H^0\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(X,E(T))\longrightarrow Q:=\operatorname{Hom}(Z^1X,T)/\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}(X^1,T)\xrightarrow{i_1^*}\operatorname{Hom}(Z^1X,T)\bigr).$$
Surjectivity is Step 4; injectivity is this homotopy construction applied to a difference whose factor extends to $X^1$. This uses no map from homotopy classes into the unquotiented Hom group.

source.place: Agent proof below proof paragraph 2: full null-homotopy induction, including its base and residual equation, and the resulting quotient identification.

proof.text: Put $A=Z^1X$, $B=X^1$, $C_0=Z^2X$, $i=i_1$, $p=p_1$. For each $g:A\to T$, apply the pushout theorem to $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C_0\to0$. Denote its exact pushout by $0\to T\xrightarrow{j_g}P_g\xrightarrow{q_g}C_0\to0$, with $v_g:B\to P_g$, $v_gi=j_gg$, and $q_gv_g=p$. Define $\partial(g)=[P_g]$. We will prove directly that $\partial$ is additive, has kernel $\operatorname{im}i^*$, and is surjective; no derived Ext or smallness hypothesis on Ext in all degrees is introduced.

source.place: Stacks homology.tex, Tag 010I (section-extensions), item (2): pushout extension. Agent expansion of the connecting-map hint for Tag 05E2 (lemma-six-term-sequence-ext).

proof.text: If $g=ui$ for some $u:B\to T$, the pair $1_T,u$ descends by the pushout universal property to $a:P_g\to T$ with $aj_g=1_T$ and $av_g=u$. Also $v_g-j_gu$ kills $i$ and hence equals $sp$ for a unique $s:C_0\to P_g$. Since $q_gsp=p$ and $p$ is epic, $q_gs=1_{C_0}$, so $P_g$ splits. Conversely, a section $s$ of $q_g$ makes $q_g(v_g-sp)=0$. The kernel description of $j_g$ in the short exact sequence gives $u:B\to T$ with $j_gu=v_g-sp$. Restriction to $A$ and cancellation of $j_g$ give $ui=g$. Thus the pushout class is split exactly when $g$ extends to $B$. We also record the full equality criterion without assuming any Baer group laws: if $\phi:P_g\to P_h$ is an isomorphism of extensions, then $\phi v_g-v_h$ has zero composite with $q_h$, so it equals $j_hu$ for a unique $u:B\to T$; restriction to $A$ gives $ui=g-h$. Conversely if $ui=g-h$, the maps $j_h:T\to P_h$ and $v_h+j_hu:B\to P_h$ agree on $A$ via $g$, so the pushout property gives $P_g\to P_h$ inducing identities on the endpoints. The five lemma makes it an isomorphism. Thus $[P_g]=[P_h]$ if and only if $g-h$ extends to $B$.

source.place: Stacks homology.tex, Tag 010I (section-extensions): explicit pushout universal-property proof of the zero-class test in the Tag 05E2 connecting map.

proof.text: For clarity, pullbacks of extensions used below are exact without assuming sections of epimorphisms. Given $0\to V\xrightarrow{j}N\xrightarrow{q}W\to0$ and $a:U\to W$, form $L=\ker((a,-q):U\oplus N\to W)$; it is the pullback, since its maps to $U,N$ satisfy $a\pi_U=q\pi_N$ and have the universal property by the kernel universal property. The map $V\to L$ with components $(0,j)$ is monic and is the kernel of $\pi_U$. To show $\pi_U$ epic, take any $b:D\to U$. By the epimorphic-refinement criterion, $ab$ lifts through $q$ after some epimorphism $D'\twoheadrightarrow D$. The pair of that lift and $b|_{D'}$ gives a lift to $L$. The same criterion now makes $\pi_U$ epic. Hence $0\to V\to L\to U\to0$ is short exact. This construction applies equally to $V=T\oplus T$.

source.place: Stacks homology.tex, Tag 010I (section-extensions), item (1), and Tags 05PK and 08N5 as stated in lem-sp-abelian-refinements: expanded proof of exactness of extension pullbacks.

proof.text: To verify additivity, form $L=P_g\times_{C_0}P_h$. Its sequence $0\to T\oplus T\to L\to C_0\to0$ is exact: project to $P_g$, using Step 9 on the extension $P_h$ to see that projection is epic; composing with $q_g$ is epic, and its kernel consists, by the two kernel universal properties, of the pairs $(j_gt_1,j_ht_2)$, namely $T\oplus T$. Push out this sequence along the sum $T\oplus T\to T$, obtaining $R$. This is the Baer sum defining addition of extension classes. The pair $(v_g,v_h):B\to L$ has restriction $(j_gg,j_hh)$ on $A$, so its composite $b:B\to R$ satisfies $bi=j_R(g+h)$. The pushout property gives $P_{g+h}\to R$ inducing identity maps on $T$ and $C_0$. The five lemma for the exact rows $0\to T\to P_{g+h}\to C_0\to0$ and $0\to T\to R\to C_0\to0$ makes it an isomorphism. Thus $\partial(g+h)=\partial(g)+\partial(h)$. Also $\partial(0)$ is split by Step 8; therefore $\partial$ preserves the specified addition and its zero fibre is $\operatorname{im}i^*$.

source.place: Stacks homology.tex, Tag 010I (section-extensions), Baer-sum construction; Tag 05QB (lemma-five-lemma). Agent-written verification of additivity rather than an invocation of the omitted proof of Tag 05E2.

proof.text: Let $0\to T\xrightarrow{j}N\xrightarrow{q}C_0\to0$ be any extension. Pull it back along $p:B\to C_0$ by Step 9, obtaining an extension of $B$ by $T$. The stated vanishing hypothesis $\operatorname{Ext}^1(B,T)=0$ makes the pullback isomorphic to the split sequence $0\to T\to T\oplus B\to B\to0$, hence split. A section of its projection to $B$, followed by its projection to $N$, is a morphism $b:B\to N$ with $qb=p$. Since $qbi=0$, there is a unique $g:A\to T$ with $jg=bi$. The pushout property gives $P_g\to N$ with components $j,b$, inducing identity maps on $T$ and $C_0$. Apply the five lemma to the two extension rows to see it is an isomorphism. Thus $\partial$ is surjective. The equality criterion of Step 8 and surjectivity give a bijection $Q\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(C_0,T)$; Step 10 shows that this bijection carries the quotient group operation to Baer addition. In particular it also proves the required abelian-group laws for Baer addition here, with the split extension as zero, and yields $Q\cong\operatorname{Ext}^1(C_0,T)$. Composing with Step 6 is the required isomorphism, and its value on $[f]$ is the pushout along the unique factor $g_f$, exactly as specified in the statement.

source.place: Stacks homology.tex, Tag 010I (section-extensions), pullback and pushout constructions; Tag 05QB. Agent-written surjectivity proof of the Tag 05E2 boundary under the given Ext-one vanishing.

proof.text: We check naturality without making any functorial claim about the arbitrary injective extensions. For a cochain map $u:Y\to X$ between admissible acyclic sources, $p_0^Xu^0=Z^1(u)p_0^Y$, so $g_{fu}=g_fZ^1(u)$. More generally for a commuting map $(a,b,c)$ between short exact rows $(A'\to B'\to C')\to(A\to B\to C)$, pushout along $ga$ in the top row has a map to $P_g\times_CC'$: its $B'$ component is $(v_gb,p')$ and its $T$ component is $(j_g,0)$. It is well defined because $bi'=ia$, and is identity on $T,C'$, hence an isomorphism by the five lemma and Step 9. Thus $\partial'(ga)=c^*\partial(g)$, which proves source naturality for the cycle rows. For $t:T\to T'$ and a map $e:E(T)\to E(T')$ with $e^0=t$, the factor satisfies $g_{ef}=tg_f$. Iterated pushout universal properties identify the extension pushed out first by $g_f$ and then by $t$ with the pushout by $tg_f$, proving coefficient naturality. Such an augmented comparison exists: apply the lifting construction of Steps 3–4 with source $E(T)$, target $E(T')$, and $g=t$ after identifying $Z^1E(T)$ with $T$ by the monomorphism $\varepsilon$. Two such comparisons are homotopic by Steps 5–6 with $u=0$ since their degree-zero components agree. In particular different injective resolutions give the same identification with Ext, and comparisons for identity and composition give the identity and composite maps. Assume the displayed Ext-one vanishing holds for each source pair under consideration. The countably many positive-degree choices make actual morphisms in the Hom product even if X is unbounded in either direction.

source.place: Agent naturality argument below proof paragraph 2, using Stacks homology.tex Tag 010I pushout/pullback universal properties and Tag 05QB; the comparison induction is already proved in Steps 3–6.
